key_insight: A quantum recurrent model detected apneic versus normal breathing with performance comparable to classical recurrent models while using far fewer parameters and few qubits.
engineering_relevance: Compact quantum recurrent architectures warrant investigation for physiological time-series classification, though these results do not establish a practical quantum advantage.
method: Use a variational classical–quantum recurrent architecture.
Classify breathing time series as apneic or normal.
Compare against classical recurrent neural networks.
evidence_signal: Across multiple real-world datasets of varying complexity, the quantum model performed best on the smallest dataset but slightly worse in the most complex setting.
watch_item: Current quantum hardware and algorithmic limitations remain barriers, and the abstract provides no numerical metrics or deployment benchmarks.
paper_title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing Detection with Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks
